advances: The exact weighted pair tree of 03229943d27787ae admits a complete, full-dimensional lattice realization with one globally affine logarithmic weight law. The realization preserves the original probability table, normalizer, reflected pair incidence, occupied parity count, and threshold, so exponential threshold-deficit compensation still fails at occupied capacity, even when the full energy is at most 9/8. Its ambient dimension is larger, and the atomic cubic sum already meets the ambient scale. Thus this is an obstruction to the occupied-capacity interface, not to the locked depth statement or its ambient scale.

proof:
We first establish the geometric and affine realization independently. The fresh-coordinate attachment of db278433c752d02f required a singleton old row to preserve injectivity of pair midpoints. Completeness itself does not require that restriction, as the following slice argument shows.

Suppose that \(D_0=Q_0\cap\mathbb Z^k\) is finite, \(Q_0=\operatorname{conv}(D_0)\), and \(v\in D_0\). Embed the old support in height zero and put
$$
D_1=(D_0\times\lbrace0\rbrace)\cup\lbrace(v,-1),(v,1)\rbrace,
\qquad Q_1=\operatorname{conv}(D_1).
$$
Every point of \(Q_1\) has last coordinate between \(-1\) and \(1\). At height \(1\) the only point is \((v,1)\), and at height \(-1\) the only point is \((v,-1)\). At height zero, any convex combination has equal coefficients on the two new points. Their combined old-coordinate contribution is a nonnegative multiple of \(v\in Q_0\), so that slice is contained in \(Q_0\times\lbrace0\rbrace\). The reverse inclusion is immediate. Thus the height-zero slice is exactly \(Q_0\times\lbrace0\rbrace\). These three heights exhaust the possible integer heights, proving \(Q_1\cap\mathbb Z^{k+1}=D_1\), for an arbitrary supported center \(v\).

The two new atoms have the same parity and have odd last coordinate, whereas every old atom has even last coordinate. Therefore their pair is the only new unordered distinct same-parity pair, its midpoint is \((v,0)\), and no old parity class changes. This adds one occupied class of size two. Every unordered supported reflected pair with integral center is necessarily a same-parity pair, since \(u+z=2j\) implies that \(u,z\) have the same coordinatewise parity. Consequently the operation adds exactly this one reflected pair and adds it only to the old row at \(v\). It works when that row already contains other pairs. Both new atoms initially have singleton rows: at either extreme height there is only one supported atom, and a noncentral reflected pair about an extreme-height atom would require two atoms at that same extreme height. If \(Q_0\) has dimension \(k\), adjoining either new atom increases the affine dimension to \(k+1\).

Suppose also that the old weights satisfy \(\log w_x=a+\beta_0\cdot x\). Given positive proposed endpoint weights \(u_+,u_-\) with \(u_+u_-=w_v^2\), choose the new slope \(\gamma=\log(u_+/w_v)\). Then the single extension
\(\log w_{(x,t)}=a+\beta_0\cdot x+\gamma t\)
preserves every old weight, gives \(u_+\) at \((v,1)\), and gives \(w_v^2/u_+=u_-\) at \((v,-1)\). Thus arbitrary positive endpoint weights with the required product are compatible with one globally affine law. Old slopes and the affine constant are unchanged.

We will also use a singleton attachment. Assume that \(0\in D_0\), and adjoin the apex \((0,1)\) to \(D_0\times\lbrace0\rbrace\). The convex hull has integer heights only zero and one, with old slice \(Q_0\times\lbrace0\rbrace\) at zero and the single apex at one. It therefore has exactly the stated integer census. The apex occupies a new singleton parity class, so this operation creates no new distinct same-parity pair and changes no reflected row except for adding the new singleton row. It increases full dimension by one. If the old affine constant is \(a\), the additional slope \(-a\) assigns weight one to the apex and preserves all old weights.

Start in \(\mathbb R^0\) with the singleton root \(0\) of raw weight \(c\). Its polytope is complete and has full dimension zero, and its affine constant is \(a=\log c\). Process levels \(\ell=0,\ldots,L\), and within each level use any fixed order of its centers. At each level-\(\ell\) center \(v\), perform \(d_\ell\) successive pair attachments, each using its own new coordinate. Give its positive endpoint the tiny weight \(w_{\ell+1}\), and its negative endpoint the large weight \(1-w_{\ell+1}\). The identity \(\alpha(t)(1-\alpha(t))=t^2\) gives the required product \(w_\ell^2\), so the affine extension just proved applies with new slope \(\log(w_{\ell+1}/w_\ell)\). Declare the new positive endpoints to be the next level's tiny atoms. The count recursion gives exactly \(N_\ell\) centers at every \(0\le\ell\le L\); the final \(N_Ld_L\) positive endpoints are terminal. This performs exactly \(m\) pair attachments.

Since \(K\ge m+1\), the integer \(f=K-m-1\) is nonnegative. After all pairs, perform \(f\) successive singleton attachments, again using fresh coordinates, each at the old origin as above. Every such apex has weight one because the affine constant remains \(\log c\). The root stays the origin with weight \(c\) throughout. There are exactly \(m+f=n\) new coordinates and the final affine law is \(w_x=c\exp(\beta\cdot x)\) for the slopes assembled in order. Repeated application of the slice arguments proves completeness at every stage, and the dimension increases by one at every stage. Thus the final \(Q\) has dimension \(n\).

At each pair attachment the new two-point parity class is disjoint from all old classes, and at each singleton attachment the new one-point class is disjoint from all old classes. Later embeddings only append zeros and never merge these classes. Starting with one root class gives exactly \(1+m+f=K\) occupied classes, with \(m\) two-point classes and \(f+1\) singleton classes. The only distinct same-parity pairs are the prescribed \(m\) pairs, whose supported midpoints are their chosen centers. Therefore the full reflected row at a level-\(\ell\) center has exactly \(1+2d_\ell\) atoms. Every other atom has a singleton reflected row. This proves the full incidence census, including all center multiplicities, without imposing midpoint injectivity.

Each pair's two endpoint weights sum to one, its endpoints are new when created, and all fillers have weight one. Consequently
\(Z=c+m+f=K-1+c\), and \(|D|=1+2m+f=K+m\). The root parity mass is \(c/Z\); each other occupied class has mass \(1/Z\). For every pair, the affine construction and its prescribed weights both give \(p_j^2=p_up_v\). Thus every summand in an oriented reflected row equals \(p_j\).

There is an exact labeled bijection from the support in 03229943d27787ae to \(D\): match the root, each successive tiny endpoint and large partner by its level, center and pair label, and the \(f\) fillers by any fixed order. The predecessor's complete pair enumeration and the enumeration just proved coincide under this bijection. It preserves each raw weight, the midpoint label of every pair, and every row's center and pair list. It need not preserve Euclidean positions. Its normalizer is the same \(Z\), so it preserves every original probability and every full-row reflected quantity as well.

For clarity, we check the threshold rather than relying only on the bijection. The elementary bounds in 03229943d27787ae are
\(w_\ell^2\le w_{\ell+1}\le(4/3)w_\ell^2<w_\ell\) and \(0<w_\ell\le c\). Every level-\(\ell\) pair has absolute score
$$
y_\ell=\frac12\log\frac{1-w_{\ell+1}}{w_{\ell+1}}
=\log\frac{1-w_{\ell+1}}{w_\ell}.
$$
For \(\ell<L\), the recurrence gives \(2w_L\le(8/3)w_{L-1}^2<w_{L-1}\). Hence \(y_\ell<\log(1/w_\ell)\le\log(1/w_{L-1})<T\). For \(\ell=L\), one has \(1-w_{L+1}>1/2\), so \(y_L>T\). Also \(T>0\) and central scores are zero. The threshold selection therefore agrees exactly with the predecessor selection. In particular it changes neither the law nor its normalizer.

One can see the scalar identity directly from the census. Write \(J=\sum_{x\in D}w_x^3\), and let \(I_{\rm ret}\) and \(I_{\rm last}\) denote the retained and final raw row increments. Since a level-\(\ell\) pair's endpoint cubes sum to \(1-3w_\ell^2\), and a degree-\(d\) center's increment is \(4d(d+1)w^3\), the exact formulas are
$$
\begin{aligned}
J&=K-1+c^3-3\sum_{\ell=0}^L N_\ell d_\ell w_\ell^2,\\
I_{\rm ret}&=4\sum_{\ell=0}^{L-1}N_\ell d_\ell(d_\ell+1)w_\ell^3,
&I_{\rm last}&=4N_Ld_L(d_L+1)w_L^3,\\
K^2b_T&=\frac{K^2}{Z^3}(J+I_{\rm ret}),
&K^2b_{\rm full}&=\frac{K^2}{Z^3}(J+I_{\rm ret}+I_{\rm last}).
\end{aligned}
$$
A tiny atom that later becomes a center contributes once to \(J\); only its row increment is added. These are precisely the predecessor's scalar formulas, with \(K=2^{n_{032}}\) replaced by the numerically identical occupied count in the new geometry. Equations (12), (14), and (16) of 03229943d27787ae, and its bound for \(e^{-T}\), now give every displayed bound for \(\delta_T\), \(\mathcal E_{\rm full}\), their ratio, and \(T\) in the statement. Their derivations depend on these exact scalar formulas and the defined parameters, not on identifying \(K\) with the new ambient capacity.

Strict positivity of the full excess also follows directly at the new occupied count. If \(r_\eta\) are the \(K\) occupied parity masses, the complete pair enumeration and exact midpoint equality give
$$
\sum_{j\in D}p_jH_{\rm full}(j)
=\sum_{x\in D}p_x^2+2\sum_{\lbrace u,v\rbrace}p_up_v
=\sum_\eta r_\eta^2>\frac1K.
$$
The strict inequality holds because the masses \(c/Z,1/Z,\ldots,1/Z\) are unequal and sum to one. Cauchy-Schwarz under the probability law \(p\) gives \(b_{\rm full}\ge(\sum_jp_jH_{\rm full}(j))^2>1/K^2\). Moreover \(H_T(j)\ge p_j\), so \(K^2\sum_jp_j^3\le K^2b_T=1-\delta_T<1\), proving atomic activity at occupied capacity.

We next check the low-full-energy claim with an explicit finite threshold in \(L\). The definition of \(d_L\) gives \(K\ge m+1\ge N_Ld_L\ge1/w_L^2\). By the accepted bound \(M_L\ge c3^{-L}\) from 03229943d27787ae,
$$
\mathcal E_{\rm full}\le\frac{200}{KM_L}
\le\frac{200w_L^2}{M_L}
\le1800\,3^Lw_L^2.
$$
The recurrence implies \(3^{L+1}w_{L+1}^2\le(16/243)3^Lw_L^2\), because \(w_L\le1/9\). Thus this bound tends to zero. Also \(w_1\le4/243\) and \(w_2\le64/177147\), so for every \(L\ge2\),
$$
\mathcal E_{\rm full}
\le16200\left(\frac{64}{177147}\right)^2
<\frac18.
$$
The final strict inequality is the integer comparison \(530841600<31381059609\) after clearing the positive denominator. Therefore \(1<K^2b_{\rm full}<9/8\) for every \(L\ge2\).

For fixed \(a>0\), the already transferred bounds imply
$$
\frac{\delta_T}{e^{-aT}\mathcal E_{\rm full}}
\ge\frac1{1818}\left(\frac23\right)^a
3^{-L}\left(\frac{27}4\right)^{a2^L}
\longrightarrow+\infty.
$$
This exceeds any fixed \(C>0\) at some finite \(L\ge2\), while retaining the proved low-full-energy regime, completeness, full dimension, and global affine law.

Finally, \(d_0=d(c)=4\) and \(L\ge1\) imply \(m\ge4\), so \(K\ge8\) and \(n=K-1\ge7\). Since \(m\le K-1\), the exact census gives \(|D|=K+m\le2K-1=2n+1\). The elementary inequality \(2n+1\le2^n\) holds for \(n\ge3\), by induction starting at \(n=3\). Hölder's inequality gives \(1=(\sum_{x\in D}p_x)^3\le|D|^2\sum_{x\in D}p_x^3\). Consequently
$$
4^n\sum_{x\in D}p_x^3
\ge\frac{4^n}{|D|^2}
\ge1.
$$
Since \(b_T\ge\sum_xp_x^3\), its ambient threshold deficit has zero positive part. This proves the stated scale boundary and explains why the exact occupied-capacity obstruction supplies no ambient-capacity or locked-depth counterexample.
statement:
For each integer \(L\ge1\), use exactly the following parameters from 03229943d27787ae. Set \(c=1/9\), and for \(0<t\le c\) put
$$
\alpha(t)=\frac{1-\sqrt{1-4t^2}}2,
\qquad d(t)=\left\lfloor\frac{1/t-1}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$
Define \(w_0=c\) and \(w_{\ell+1}=\alpha(w_\ell)\) for \(0\le\ell\le L\). Set \(N_0=1\), and for \(0\le\ell<L\) set \(d_\ell=d(w_\ell)\) and \(N_{\ell+1}=N_\ell d_\ell\). Put \(M_\ell=N_\ell w_\ell\) for \(0\le\ell\le L\), and define
$$
\begin{aligned}
d_L&=\left\lceil\frac1{N_Lw_L^2}\right\rceil,
&m&=\sum_{\ell=0}^L N_\ell d_\ell,\\
K&=2^{\lceil\log_2(m+1)\rceil},
&f&=K-m-1,\\
n&=m+f=K-1,
&T&=\log\frac1{2w_L}.
\end{aligned}
$$
Here \(K\) has the same numerical value as the ambient capacity in 03229943d27787ae, whose dimension will be denoted \(n_{032}=\lceil\log_2(m+1)\rceil\). In the realization below, \(n=K-1\) is the new ambient dimension and \(K\) is the number of occupied parity classes. Thus \(K=2^{n_{032}}\), whereas in general \(K\ne2^n\). The symbols \(w_\ell,N_\ell,d_\ell,M_\ell,m,T\) and every assigned raw weight have exactly their predecessor meanings.

There exist a finite support \(D\subset\mathbb Z^n\), a full-dimensional lattice polytope \(Q=\operatorname{conv}(D)\), and a vector \(\beta\in\mathbb R^n\) such that \(D=Q\cap\mathbb Z^n\) and the raw law is the single affine exponential law \(w_x=c\exp(\beta\cdot x)\) on all of \(D\). The origin is the root and has raw weight \(c\). The support has exactly this weighted midpoint census: there are \(N_\ell\) tiny centers at level \(\ell\), for \(0\le\ell\le L\), of raw weight \(w_\ell\), each the midpoint of \(d_\ell\) distinct pairs. Each such pair has a new tiny endpoint of raw weight \(w_{\ell+1}\) and a new large endpoint of raw weight \(1-w_{\ell+1}\). Tiny endpoints at levels at most \(L\) are exactly the next centers; the level-\(L+1\) tiny endpoints are terminal. There are also exactly \(f\) singleton fillers of raw weight one. These are all atoms and all unordered distinct same-parity pairs. In particular center multiplicities are allowed, every parity class has at most two atoms, and exactly \(K\) parity classes are occupied.

Use the original normalizer and original positive probability law
$$
Z=\sum_{x\in D}w_x=K-1+c,
\qquad p_x=\frac{w_x}{Z}.
$$
For each \(j\in D\), let \(R_j=\lbrace x\in D:2j-x\in D\rbrace\), and define the symmetric threshold row
\(R_{T,j}=\lbrace x\in R_j:|(1/2)\log(p_x/p_{2j-x})|\le T\rbrace\).
The central atom is always in \(R_{T,j}\). Use the genuine oriented reflected sums, with the central term counted once:
$$
\begin{aligned}
H_T(j)&=\sum_{x\in R_{T,j}}\sqrt{p_xp_{2j-x}},
&b_T&=\sum_{j\in D}p_jH_T(j)^2,\\
H_{\rm full}(j)&=\sum_{x\in R_j}\sqrt{p_xp_{2j-x}},
&b_{\rm full}&=\sum_{j\in D}p_jH_{\rm full}(j)^2.
\end{aligned}
$$
Every pair satisfies \(p_j^2=p_up_v\) at its midpoint. The threshold retains exactly the pairs of levels \(0,\ldots,L-1\) and discards exactly the level-\(L\) pairs. Consequently these \(H_T,H_{\rm full},b_T,b_{\rm full}\), including their original normalization, equal the corresponding labeled quantities in 03229943d27787ae. If \(d_T(j)\) and \(d_{\rm full}(j)\) are the retained and full pair counts at \(j\), then \(H_T(j)=(1+2d_T(j))p_j\) and \(H_{\rm full}(j)=(1+2d_{\rm full}(j))p_j\).

At the occupied count \(K\), put \(\delta_T=1-K^2b_T\) and \(\mathcal E_{\rm full}=K^2b_{\rm full}-1\). Then
$$
\begin{aligned}
\delta_T&\ge\frac{1-c^3}{K}>0,
&0<\mathcal E_{\rm full}&\le\frac{200}{KM_L},\\
\frac{\delta_T}{\mathcal E_{\rm full}}&\ge\frac{3^{-L}}{1818},
&e^{-T}&\le\frac32\left(\frac4{27}\right)^{2^L}.
\end{aligned}
$$
In addition \(K^2\sum_{x\in D}p_x^3<1\), \(\mathcal E_{\rm full}\longrightarrow0\) as \(L\to\infty\), and \(1<K^2b_{\rm full}<9/8\) for every \(L\ge2\). For every \(a>0\) and \(C>0\), some finite \(L\ge2\) therefore gives a complete full-dimensional globally affine law satisfying
$$
(1-K^2b_T)_+>C e^{-aT}(K^2b_{\rm full}-1),
\qquad K^2b_{\rm full}<\frac98.
$$
The ambient calibration is different: \(n\ge7\), \(|D|=K+m\le2n+1\le2^n\), and \(4^n\sum_{x\in D}p_x^3\ge1\). Hence \((1-4^n b_T)_+=0\). No ambient-capacity obstruction, and no counterexample to the locked mixed-integer depth statement, is asserted.
